page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores using an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. The system is equipped with 224.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU accelerators, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. The processor includes hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and SHA extensions, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-standard-56 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory performance. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10%, complemented by strong multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench. Software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing workloads all register in the top 25% of tested systems. However, single-threaded operations, such as Gzip compression and Bzip3 decompression, perform in the average tier. Large-block memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations also fall within the middle 50% of benchmarked servers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high-density allocation of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and memory without the added expense of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. This makes it a balanced option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local solid-state drives. The server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, database operations, and medium-scale language model text generation.
